newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Lack of urgency costs Wellington.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Lack of urgency costs Wellington.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Oct 14 - Wellington were again left to rue some badly needed urgency after losing 18-10 to Otago in their final NPC first-division rugby match at Carisbrook yesterday, NZPA reports.
The loss left Wellington short of a coveted spot in the semifinals, although fifth place was their best effort for the past eight seasons and a considerable improvement on last year's seventh.

Otago, in the early stages of development under new coach Glen Ross, were unexceptional but willing to fight for what they could get, and they had outstanding flanker Josh Kronfeld and halfback Stu Forster to point them in the right direction.
Wellington didn't show the same enthusiasm or tactical nous in the difficult southerly conditions, and paid the price.
Enthusiasm would have gone a long way to curing their biggest failing: an inability to retain the ball and bring continuity to their game.
Wellington turned the ball over to Otago with rare abandon, 26 times in total, and 16 times in the second half.

Wellington's faults were basic. There was no protection or support of the ball carrier; they were too flat running on to the ball; players moved in ones and twos rather than in groups and there was a lack of urgency overall.
Added to that, their kicking in the second half was poor which left Wellington playing much of the game in the wrong part of the field.
"The one thing we wanted was ball control and ball retention and we did neither," said Wellington coach Frank Walker.
"That was the winning and losing of the game. The support of the ball carrier was not there. That seems to be the story of our game."
Walker is at a loss to figure out why the players were unable to explode on to the park and attack with a will. Only flanker Inoke Afeaki really kept up his standards.
"Urgency is basically up to the individual. If it's not in there, you'll never put it there. It's very hard to coach urgency into players," he said.
Walker's position now looks very much up in air, although captain Jason O'Halloran gave the coach a strong endorsement after Sunday's game and asked for one more year for the team management.
